items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I know Dizzy played some gigs with me out of New York

ctx.x: sort of relationship did you have to that? Did it influence you? Because I remember, for instance, Louis really put it down, and some of the older musicians who had been innovators in their time suddenly decided bebop was not music, and --

Tom, I hate to say this, but bebop never moved me. Number one is I couldn't play it, and I used to fool around and try to play some things. I learned in later years to play it a little, but I was told to stick more or less to the swing, you know? And while I admired Charlie Parker.
